output.brief: The slowdown comes mainly from one change in the May credit policy refresh. Property appraisals are now mandatory in full for loans between $150k and $500k. Before, a quick desktop valuation was allowed. A full appraisal takes about 8.6 days, against about 1.2 for a desktop one. The valuer's speed hasn't changed. The valuation stage for property-secured loans rose from about 1.7 days in April to 7.6 in June and 8.4 in August. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, which is near their March level. New hires aren't slowing things down, since document collection at their branches matches the rest. Corvane caused some April disruption, but it doesn't explain the sustained rise. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing times. Withdrawals are partly an artifact: files with no upload for 30 days are now auto-closed as withdrawn. Only 14 of 73 closures were customers who financed elsewhere. I'm fairly confident, about 85–90%. I recommend taking the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee, so it can decide whether to amend §6.3. Don't withhold the Corvane payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard.
